channel.title: Marcos Oliveira: notes from 15 years of trigger electronics
channel.description: One post per problem I worked on in FPGA and trigger electronics, with the details I wish I had found written down.

item.title: One description for firmware and software registers: Wishlist
item.description: Wishlist turns a YAML list of registers into VHDL and SystemVerilog packages, address decoders, an IPbus table, an HTML map and a runtime robot, so firmware and software always agree.

item.title: Architecting the Global Trigger multiplexer
item.description: The firmware architecture of the ATLAS Global Trigger multiplexer: FIFOs, a full-mesh time-multiplexed switch, die-crossing limits in multi-die FPGAs, and generated registers.

item.title: Starting with HLS: from a logic gate to a FIR filter
item.description: A first session on high-level synthesis, from one AND gate through bit widths, pipelining and loop unrolling to a pipelined FIR filter, as taught at the US AHEAD bootcamp.

item.title: Talking between FPGAs on the same board
item.description: 240 LVDS links at 1.12 Gb/s between the three processing FPGAs of the ATLAS gFEX, with automatic sampling-phase search, word alignment and in-system margin scans.

item.title: High-level synthesis in production: calorimeter firmware
item.description: How part of the ATLAS Liquid Argon calorimeter trigger firmware was rewritten in HLS, with a sparse switch matrix and resource-shared encoders, and is now used for physics.

item.title: Timing distribution for the High-Luminosity LHC
item.description: Jitter, phase uncertainty and temperature drift of the LHC clock in ATLAS, what each means for the Liquid Argon calorimeter, and a non-disruptive clock mode.

item.title: Sorting networks in RTL and in HLS: SNpy
item.description: A 352-input, 16-output sorting network in 32 steps for the ATLAS muon trigger, found with the SNpy package and implemented in both VHDL and high-level synthesis.

item.title: Testing 300 transceivers without touching them: IBERTpy
item.description: IBERTpy automates bit-error-rate tests, eye scans, mask checks and reporting for boards with hundreds of high-speed serial links.

item.title: Checking PCB schematics with a script: PCBpy
item.description: PCBpy reads the netlist of a board and generates VHDL wrappers, pin and polarity constraints and verification reports for its FPGAs.

item.title: Making transceiver latency deterministic
item.description: Measuring and reducing the latency and latency uncertainty of FPGA multi-gigabit transceivers: from 67 ns to 50 ns, with a fixed transmitter latency.

item.title: Synchronising more than 100 serial links in one FPGA
item.description: A dual-port-memory block that brings 208 serial inputs into one clock domain with low, fixed latency, calibrated once, for the ATLAS MUCTPI.

item.title: Teaching a trigger where the muons are
item.description: How the ATLAS muon trigger interface was upgraded for LHC Run 2 to send the position of each muon over outputs built for 40 MHz, overclocked to 320 Mb/s.

item.title: Building the first Latin American power-line modem
item.description: FPGA blocks for the physical layer of an HS-OFDM power-line modem at UFJF: a multiplier-free QAM detector, a low-cost timing synchroniser, verification against the model, and a Verilog course.
